objective: Select one reachable orientation schedule for the unchanged consecutive-left high-clearance position route before any new dynamic transition panel.

single_variable_family.name: consecutive_left_orientation_schedule
changed: the waypoint stage over which the left TCP orientation changes from the unchanged 90-degree grasp orientation to the unchanged 60-degree transit orientation
unchanged: vertical, lateral, and descent Cartesian position waypoints
eight position waypoints per translational segment
start grasp orientation and final transit orientation
IK solver, initializations, sample count, iteration count, position tolerance, rotation tolerance, and joint limits
source reset distribution, bowl order, arm assignment, grasp, transport, placement, release, safety, collision, success, and stability semantics
physics and policy clocks, action mapping, gripper mapping, cameras, assets, datasets, models, evaluation seeds, and training configuration

candidates_in_order.orientation_schedule: vertical grasp; one fixed-position jump to transit at prior high XY; lateral transit; descent transit
candidates_in_order.expected_role: must reproduce the predecessor failure signature

candidates_in_order.orientation_schedule: vertical grasp; SLERP grasp-to-transit across the eight high-clearance lateral waypoints; descent transit
vertical grasp; lateral grasp; SLERP grasp-to-transit across the eight descent waypoints
vertical grasp; SLERP alpha 0-to-0.5 across lateral and 0.5-to-1.0 across descent

matrix.selection_rule: Among candidates that pass every waypoint under unchanged IK tolerances, select the candidate with the greatest minimum normalized IK slack; break an exact tie by the frozen candidate order.

downstream_policy.accepted_terminal_action: Freeze the selected orientation schedule in a new dynamic-transition work package and a project newer than v123.
downstream_policy.rejected_terminal_action: Preserve negative evidence and redesign one position-route variable; do not run another dynamic panel.

claim_boundary: This matrix can establish only kinematic reachability of a predeclared orientation schedule after one scripted CPU setup trajectory. It cannot prove collision avoidance, dynamic tracking, task success, training-data quality, learned-policy improvement, G3 passage, AMD/ROCm execution, hardware validity, or real-robot safety.
